## Quick decision guide

| You need…                                                     | Reach for                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hover colour, focus ring, spinner                             | CSS transitions / keyframes                                       |
| One element fades or slides when it enters or leaves          | `animate.enter` / `animate.leave` (or `moveEnter` / `moveLeave`)  |
| A panel that must finish leaving before its parent is removed | Movement: `*movePresence`                                         |
| A list where rows are added, removed and reordered            | Movement: `*movePresenceFor`                                      |
| A card that changes between idle / selected / error states    | Movement: `moveVariants` or `moveAnimation`                       |
| Staggered reveal of siblings                                  | Movement: `moveStagger`                                           |
| Progress bound to scroll position                             | Movement: `moveScroll` (or CSS `scroll-timeline` where supported) |
| A single custom effect, nothing reused                        | Raw WAAPI                                                         |

## CSS transitions and keyframes

If the motion is a function of a class or pseudo-class — a hover colour, a focus ring, a loading spinner, a menu that slides when a class is toggled — write CSS. It costs no JavaScript, works before hydration and is the easiest thing to maintain. Movement does not try to replace this, and you can mix both freely.

```css title=button.css
.button {
  transition:
    background-color 150ms ease,
    transform 150ms ease;
}
.button:hover {
  background-color: var(--accent-strong);
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .button {
    transition: none;
  }
}
```

## Angular's native `animate.enter` and `animate.leave`

Since Angular 20.2 the framework can apply CSS classes while a node enters and leaves the DOM, and `@angular/animations` is deprecated in favour of it. For many apps this covers the common case: each element has its own self-contained enter or leave effect described in CSS. It needs no extra dependency, and you should prefer it when that is all you need.

```html title=panel.html
<!-- Angular adds the class on enter and waits for the animation to finish before removing the node on leave. -->
@if (open()) {
<section animate.enter="panel-enter" animate.leave="panel-leave">Details</section>
}
```

What it does not give you is coordination: no built-in way to hold a parent until all children have finished leaving, to reverse a keyed list item that is re-added while it is exiting, to stagger by DOM order, or to animate between two states of one element when a signal changes.

## Angular Movement

Movement earns its place when motion is driven by state and must be coordinated:

- **State to state** — `moveVariants` and `[moveAnimation]` animate to a new target whenever a signal changes.
- **Presence** — `*movePresence` and `*movePresenceFor` keep a view (or each keyed row) mounted until every leave animation finishes, including nested children and revival mid-exit.
- **Orchestration** — `moveStagger` and variant `staggerChildren` for DOM-order delays.
- **Interaction feedback** — `moveWhileHover`, `moveWhileTap` and `moveWhileFocus`, with proper touch semantics.
- **Scroll, springs, SVG and signals** — `moveScroll`, `moveSpringValue`, `movePathDraw` and `moveTransform`.
- **Imperative sequences** — `MoveAnimator`, with automatic reduced-motion handling and SSR no-ops.

```html title=card.html
<ul>
  <li
    *movePresenceFor="let item of items(); trackBy: byId"
    move="fade-up"
    [moveWhileHover]="{ y: [0, -2] }"
  >
    {{ item.label }}
  </li>
</ul>
```

## Raw WAAPI

`element.animate()` is fine for one isolated effect. You then own reduced motion, cancellation, committing final styles and server-side no-ops. Movement's engines and [`MoveAnimator`](/docs/reference/move-animator) are thin wrappers that do these things consistently.

## Honest trade-offs

> [!WARNING]
> Movement plays on the Web Animations API, which depends on hydration: anything it animates in from a hidden state needs the app to have started. For above-the-fold entrances that must paint immediately, prefer CSS. See [Accessibility and troubleshooting](/docs/accessibility).

- It is an additional dependency (a small, tree-shakeable one). If CSS or native enter and leave cover your needs, you do not need it.
- Layout, drag and smooth-scroll APIs are still **experimental**. Prefer native scrolling.
